lem-equi-lipschitz-curves-in-compact-euc:
## Statement

Let $d\ge1$, $T>0$, and let $C\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be nonempty, compact, and closed. Let $M\ge0$. If $u_j:[0,T]\to C$ satisfies
$$\|u_j(t)-u_j(s)\|_2\le M|t-s|\qquad(j\ge1,\ s,t\in[0,T]),$$
then some subsequence converges uniformly to a map $u:[0,T]\to C$ with the same Lipschitz bound.
lem-projection-onto-closed-convex-set-is:
## Statement

Let $C\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be nonempty, closed, and convex, and let $P_C(y)$ denote the unique nearest point in $C$ to $y$. Then
$$\|P_C(u)-P_C(v)\|_2\le\|u-v\|_2\qquad(u,v\in\mathbb R^d).$$
alg-one-dimensional-first-impact-with-re:
## Definition

Input a gap $q\ge0$, velocity $v\in\mathbb R$, constant acceleration $a\in\mathbb R$, step horizon $h>0$, mass $m>0$, restitution $e\in[0,1]$, and a finite root-search budget $B\in\mathbb N$. Define the free-flight gap and velocity by $g(s)=q+sv+\tfrac12as^2$ and $w(s)=v+as$ for $0\le s\le h$. Return one of `impact`, `free-flight`, or `unresolved` as follows.

1. If $q=0$ and $v<0$, set the event time $s=0$.
2. Otherwise find all distinct roots $s\in(0,h]$ of $g(s)=0$ for which $w(s)<0$, in increasing order. The root search must certify that this list is complete within budget $B$. If it cannot, return `unresolved`.
3. If the list is nonempty, take its first root, set $v^-=w(s)$ and $J=-m(1+e)v^-$, and return `impact` with event time $s$, contact gap $0$, impulse $J$, and post-impact velocity $v^+=-e v^-$.
4. If there is no incoming root, certify $g(r)\ge0$ for every $r\in[0,h]$. If this fails or cannot be certified within $B$, return `unresolved`; otherwise return `free-flight` with endpoint $(g(h),w(h))$ and impulse $0$.

The procedure stops after this first event and returns at the event time. It does not integrate the post-impact mode, sustained contact, or repeated impacts. Its exact algebraic branch uses at most two distinct quadratic roots; a numerical root solver must report a certificate or `unresolved` when its budget is exhausted.
thm-frictionless-sphere-binary-impact-im:
## Statement

Let two spheres of radii $r_1,r_2>0$ and masses $m_1,m_2>0$ have centers $q_1,q_2\in\mathbb R^d$ at contact, so $\|q_1-q_2\|_2=r_1+r_2$. Let $n=(q_1-q_2)/(r_1+r_2)$ be the unit normal pointing from center $2$ to center $1$. Suppose the pre-impact relative normal velocity is $v_n=\langle v_1^- - v_2^-,n\rangle<0$. For prescribed restitution $e\in[0,1]$, put
$$\alpha=\frac1{m_1}+\frac1{m_2},\qquad J=-\frac{(1+e)v_n}{\alpha},\qquad v_1^+=v_1^-+\frac{J}{m_1}n,\quad v_2^+=v_2^- -\frac{J}{m_2}n.$$
Then $J>0$, total linear momentum is conserved, the post-impact relative normal velocity is $-e v_n$, each tangential velocity is unchanged, and
$$K^+-K^-=-\frac{(1-e^2)v_n^2}{2(1/m_1+1/m_2)}\le0,$$
where $K^\pm=\tfrac12m_1\|v_1^\pm\|_2^2+\tfrac12m_2\|v_2^\pm\|_2^2$. This is a single frictionless binary impulse law; it asserts no existence or uniqueness for simultaneous or frictional multi-contact.
lem-projected-euler-projection-residual-:
## Statement

Let $C\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be nonempty, closed, and convex. If $y\in\mathbb R^d$, $\varepsilon\ge0$, and $p\in C$ satisfy
$$\sup_{z\in C}\langle y-p,z-p\rangle\le\varepsilon^2,$$
then $\|p-P_C(y)\|_2\le\varepsilon$.
thm-first-impact-step-complementarity-mo:
## Statement

For any resolved output of [[alg-one-dimensional-first-impact-with-restitution]], let $q_*$ be the reported gap (zero at an impact, the free-flight endpoint gap otherwise), let $J$ be the reported impulse, and let $v_*$ be the reported endpoint velocity. Then $q_*\ge0$, $J\ge0$, and $q_*J=0$. On a free-flight branch, $J=0$ and $m v_*=m v+mah$. On an impact branch at time $s$, with incoming velocity $v^-=v+as$, the post-impact velocity satisfies $m v^+=m v^-+J$ and
$$\frac12m(v^+)^2-\frac12m(v^-)^2=-\frac12m(1-e^2)(v^-)^2\le0.$$
When $a=0$, the full resolved step has nonincreasing kinetic energy. For $a\ne0$, the displayed energy statement concerns only the instantaneous impact jump; work during free flight is not covered by it.
lem-sphere-contact-guard-normal-and-rese:
## Statement

Use the Euclidean norm on the full state $z=(q_1,\ldots,q_P,v_1,\ldots,v_P)$ of $P\ge2$ spheres in $\mathbb R^d$. Fix a pair $i<j$, positive masses $m_i,m_j$, positive radii $r_i,r_j$, and a fixed restitution coefficient $e\in[0,1]$. Put
$$d_{ij}=q_i-q_j,\quad n(z)=\frac{d_{ij}}{\|d_{ij}\|_2},\quad \gamma(z)=\|d_{ij}\|_2-r_i-r_j,$$
$$\alpha=m_i^{-1}+m_j^{-1},\quad \kappa=\frac{1+e}{\alpha},\quad \beta=\sqrt{m_i^{-2}+m_j^{-2}}.$$
Extend the binary reset formula of [[thm-frictionless-sphere-binary-impact-impulse-laws]] to every state with $d_{ij}\ne0$ by setting $J(z)=-\kappa\langle v_i-v_j,n(z)\rangle$, replacing $v_i$ by $v_i+J(z)n(z)/m_i$ and $v_j$ by $v_j-J(z)n(z)/m_j$, and leaving all other coordinates unchanged. Denote this time-independent reset extension by $R(z)$.

The functions $\gamma,n,R$ are $C^1$ on the open set $d_{ij}\ne0$. For two states $z,z'$ with both pair distances at least $\sigma>0$ and both relative velocity norms at most $V\ge0$,
$$|\gamma(z)-\gamma(z')|\le\sqrt2\|z-z'\|_2,\qquad
\|n(z)-n(z')\|_2\le\frac{2\sqrt2}{\sigma}\|z-z'\|_2,$$
$$\|R(z)-R(z')\|_2\le L_R\|z-z'\|_2,\qquad
L_R:=1+\sqrt2\,\beta\kappa\left(1+\frac{4V}{\sigma}\right).$$
These pairwise bounds do not require a convex collision-free state set. Along a differentiable smooth segment with $q_k'=v_k$,
$$\frac d{dt}\gamma(z(t))=\langle n(z(t)),v_i(t)-v_j(t)\rangle.$$
The normal bound $2/\sigma$ applies to differences of the relative vectors $d_{ij}$; its full-state version includes the factor $\sqrt2$. This extension does not assert that an approximate state is exactly at contact or that an event exists.
alg-event-driven-frictionless-sphere-con:
## Definition

**Inputs.** A dimension $d\ge1$; $P\ge2$ spheres with centers $q_i$, velocities
$v_i$, masses $m_i>0$, radii $r_i>0$ and fixed restitution coefficients
$e_{ij}\in[0,1]$; an initial state and horizon $T>0$; a positive time-bracket
tolerance $\epsilon_{\rm time}$, a separate positive guard-residual tolerance
$\epsilon_{\rm guard}$, an event-separation bound $\delta>0$, a certified
finite event-count bound $N_{\rm evt}\in\mathbb N$, an event budget
$B\in\mathbb N$, and a finite-budget
certificate provider. The smooth state field has $q_i'=v_i$ and a $C^1$ force
field on a neighborhood of an admitted compact tube. Throughout each certified
incoming/outgoing tube every pair distance is at least a stated $\sigma>0$.
The provider supplies finite relative-velocity bounds $V$ and state/field
bounds wherever they are used below.

The provider is an explicit admissible input, not an automatically constructed
oracle for arbitrary $C^1$ fields. It must supply the following valid data,
with any failed or undecidable certificate test returning `unresolved`.

1. From the last reported reset, a continuous accumulated dense reconstruction
   $U$ and a certified uniform error $\eta_{\rm loc}$ relative to the exact
   smooth-mode solution launched from that reported state. It also supplies
   a bound $E$ on the discrepancy from the reference hybrid trajectory at
   the same aligned segment-start time, initially $E=0$. On a common mode
   prefix of duration $H$, supply a state-Lipschitz constant $L$ and the common
   solution/tube hypotheses of [[lem-ode-flow-lipschitz-on-a-tube]], and use
   $\eta_{\rm ref}=\eta_{\rm loc}+e^{LH}E$. A finite cover of certified
   convex mode tubes may be used with its propagated bounds. A Jacobian bound
   on a nonconvex compact set alone is not a substitute for these hypotheses.

2. For every pair $i<j$, exact-reference guard enclosures for
   $\gamma_{ij}(t)=\|q_i(t)-q_j(t)\|_2-r_i-r_j$, and a certificate covering
   the whole interval since the last processed event that excludes earlier
   unreported incoming roots. A sufficient explicit sampling assumption may
   replace a range cover only when its stated variation/domain assumptions
   justify the same exclusion. Endpoint signs or an unsuccessful sign scan
   alone do not certify absence. Dense-guard enclosures must include the
   state-error inflation $\sqrt2\eta_{\rm ref}$ as well as guard-evaluation
   and rounding error; the bound follows from
   [[lem-sphere-contact-guard-normal-and-reset-lipschitz-bounds]].

3. For each candidate event, a bracket $[a,b]$ containing exactly one root
   $\tau$ of the exact reference guard, with
   $b-a\le\epsilon_{\rm time}$ and $b-a<\delta/3$. On the entire bracket,
   certify the incoming inequality
   $\dot\gamma_{ij}(t)\le-\nu<0$, not just a derivative value at its root.
   Supply disjoint ordering certificates identifying the unique earliest
   event among all pairs. A grazing/uncertain derivative, ambiguous overlap
   or simultaneous multi-contact is unresolved; lexicographic inspection
   does not settle physical simultaneous impacts.

4. At $\widehat\tau=b$, a certified bound
   $\epsilon_{\rm obs}\ge|\gamma_{ij}(\widehat\tau,U(\widehat\tau))|$
   with $\epsilon_{\rm obs}\le\epsilon_{\rm guard}$. The provider includes
   all evaluation errors in this bound. The actual lag is nonnegative and
   bounded by
   $$\Delta:=\min\left\{b-a,\frac{\sqrt2\eta_{\rm ref}+\epsilon_{\rm obs}}{\nu}\right\}$$
   by [[lem-transverse-hybrid-event-time-error]]. Require certified bounds
   $M^-,M^+$ for the incoming/outgoing fields through this lag, and reset
   domain/tube checks. For the selected pair use the state-reset bound $L_R$
   from [[lem-sphere-contact-guard-normal-and-reset-lipschitz-bounds]], with
   a velocity bound valid for both compared reset inputs. This reset has no
   explicit time dependence. Supply a separate $\epsilon_R\ge0$ if the reset
   formula itself is evaluated inexactly.

5. A certificate that the matched isolated exact events have separation at
   least $\delta$ and count at most $N_{\rm evt}$. Specify whether a horizon
   endpoint impact is included in that count or the endpoint is reported as
   a pre-impact state. Process an initial enabled root at most once. Missing
   endpoint/count/separation bookkeeping is unresolved. In particular $e=0$
   does not establish another isolated transverse event after the reset.

**Procedure.** Request these certificates for every unordered pair on each
smooth segment, inspecting the pair list in increasing lexicographic order.
If the provider certifies no further event before the chosen horizon endpoint,
return that segment, its accumulated error bound and its certificates. Otherwise
select the certified unique earliest pair and use its upper bracket endpoint
$\widehat\tau=b$. Evaluate the binary impulse formula of
[[thm-frictionless-sphere-binary-impact-impulse-laws]] as the smooth reset
extension at $U(b)$; keep positions fixed and update only the selected two
velocities. The impulse theorem's exact contact/momentum/restitution/energy
laws concern the reference exact incoming contact. A reported approximate
state is not asserted to be exactly at contact; its reset error is recorded.

By [[lem-reset-error-after-a-mistimed-hybrid-event]], set the next aligned
reset-state error bound to
$$E\leftarrow L_R\eta_{\rm ref}+(L_RM^-+M^+)\Delta+\epsilon_R.$$
The outgoing $M^+\Delta$ term accounts for the reference trajectory's flow
from its earlier true reset to the reported time. Restart the smooth integrator
at $b$ with the reported reset state, discard the previous local reconstruction,
and start the next accumulated dense-error ledger. These recurrences compare
only matched smooth-mode prefixes and post-reset states at aligned times; they
make no same-clock state-error assertion between an exact jump and its later
reported jump.

Stop at $T$ or after $B$ accepted events. If another event is required after
the budget, return `unresolved` with the certified partial trajectory. A
completed run requires $B\ge N_{\rm evt}$ or a certified no-further-event result
before the budget is exhausted. Any missing enclosure, margin, ordering,
separation/count or restart certificate, failed reset domain, or depleted
provider budget returns `unresolved` without an event-absence claim.

The search enumerates $P(P-1)/2$ pairs per smooth segment. Root-solve guard
evaluations, dense reintegration and restart-error calculation are charged
separately from one inspection per pair. No neighbor-search acceleration,
frictional solver, or simultaneous-contact solver is specified.
def-projected-contact-dynamics-and-euler:
## Definition

Let $d\ge1$, let $C\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be nonempty, closed, and convex, and let $P_C(y)$ be the unique nearest point in $C$ to $y$, whose existence and uniqueness are [[thm-nearest-point-in-a-nonempty-closed-convex-set]]. For $x\in C$, set
$$N_C(x)=\{n\in\mathbb R^d:\langle n,z-x\rangle\le0\text{ for every }z\in C\};$$
for $x\notin C$, set $N_C(x)=\varnothing$. On $C$ this is the outward normal cone of [[def-kkt-residual-and-normal-cone]]. The projection variational inequality of [[lem-projection-onto-a-closed-convex-set-has-the-variational-inequality]] says $P_C(y)=p$ exactly when $p\in C$ and $y-p\in N_C(p)$.

For $T>0$, a solution of the projected contact dynamics with forcing $f:[0,T]\times C\to\mathbb R^d$ and initial state $x_0\in C$ is an absolutely continuous map $x:[0,T]\to C$ satisfying
$$f(t,x(t))-\dot x(t)\in N_C(x(t))\quad\text{for almost every }t\in[0,T].$$
Equivalently, $\dot x(t)+N_C(x(t))\ni f(t,x(t))$. For an integer $N\ge1$, put $h=T/N$, $t_k=kh$, and define the exact explicit projection Euler nodes by
$$x_{k+1}=P_C\bigl(x_k+h f(t_k,x_k)\bigr),\qquad k=0,\ldots,N-1,$$
starting from $x_0$. Its affine interpolant joins consecutive nodes linearly on each interval $[t_k,t_{k+1}]$.
lem-naive-all-pairs-collision-search-has:
## Statement

For $P\ge2$ spheres, the naive search that evaluates every unordered pair guard exactly once per smooth segment performs $P(P-1)/2$ pair-guard evaluations. Thus it uses $O(P^2)$ pair checks; this count excludes the cost of each certified event solve, dense reintegration, and restart-error certificate. With zero or one sphere the pair list is empty, but the event-driven algorithm is defined for $P\ge2$.
lem-normal-cone-maximal-monotone-and-pro:
## Statement

Let $C\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be nonempty, closed, and convex, and let $N_C$ have the convention of [[def-projected-contact-dynamics-and-euler-step]]. An operator $A:\mathbb R^d\rightrightarrows\mathbb R^d$ is **monotone** if $\langle u-v,x-y\rangle\ge0$ for all $u\in A(x)$ and $v\in A(y)$; it is **maximal monotone** if its graph has no proper monotone graph extension. Then $N_C$ is maximal monotone. For every $\tau>0$ and $y\in\mathbb R^d$, there is a unique $p$ with $y-p\in\tau N_C(p)$, and that point is $P_C(y)$. Equivalently, $(I+\tau N_C)^{-1}=P_C$.
alg-certified-projected-euler-method:
## Definition

Input a nonempty compact convex set $C\subseteq\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge1$, an exact force evaluator $f:[0,T]\times C\to\mathbb R^d$, $T>0$, integer step count $N\ge1$, initial state $x_0\in C$, tolerances $\varepsilon_k\ge0$, and finite solver budgets $B_k\in\mathbb N$ for $k=0,\ldots,N-1$. Set $h=T/N$ and $t_k=kh$. At step $k$, form
$$y_k=x_k+h f(t_k,x_k).$$
Ask the projection solver for $p_{k+1}\in C$ and a certificate that
$$\sup_{z\in C}\langle y_k-p_{k+1},z-p_{k+1}\rangle\le\varepsilon_k^2.$$
If the solver does not return a feasible candidate and a valid certificate within budget $B_k$, stop and return `unresolved` with the valid prefix $x_0,\ldots,x_k$. Otherwise set $x_{k+1}=p_{k+1}$ and continue. After all $N$ steps, return `complete`, the nodes, their affine interpolant, and the per-step tolerances. The definition assumes exact force evaluations and exact verification of the displayed residual; arithmetic and force-evaluation errors are not included. With $\varepsilon_k=0$, a successful step satisfies the exact projection-Euler recurrence by [[lem-projected-euler-projection-residual-certificate]].

The algorithm makes at most $N$ solver calls and uses the stated per-call budgets. Failure to certify a projection is reported; no convergence or accuracy is inferred from a solver's unverified stopping tolerance.
lem-projected-contact-solutions-are-uniq:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice. Let $T>0$, let $C\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be nonempty, closed, and convex, and let $f:[0,T]\times C\to\mathbb R^d$ satisfy $\|f(t,x)-f(t,y)\|_2\le L\|x-y\|_2$ for all $t,x,y$, with $L\ge0$. Any two absolutely continuous solutions of the projected dynamics of [[def-projected-contact-dynamics-and-euler-step]] with the same initial state agree on $[0,T]$.
thm-projected-euler-existence-uniqueness:
## Statement

Let $d\ge1$, let $C\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be nonempty, compact, and convex, let $T>0$, and let $x_0\in C$. Suppose $f:[0,T]\times C\to\mathbb R^d$ is Lipschitz in the explicit sense
$$\|f(t,x)-f(s,y)\|_2\le L\bigl(|t-s|+\|x-y\|_2\bigr)$$
for some $L\ge0$ and all $s,t,x,y$. Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice. Then the projected inclusion
$$x(0)=x_0,\qquad f(t,x(t))-\dot x(t)\in N_C(x(t))\quad\text{for almost every }t\in[0,T]$$
has a unique absolutely continuous solution $x:[0,T]\to C$. For each integer $N\ge1$, define $h=T/N$, $t_k=kh$, and the exact projection Euler nodes by
$$x_{k+1}=P_C\bigl(x_k+h f(t_k,x_k)\bigr),\qquad k=0,\ldots,N-1.$$
Their affine interpolants converge uniformly to $x$ as $N\to\infty$. Countable Choice is used for the almost-everywhere statements and null-set unions; Dependent Choice enters through the absolutely-continuous FTC supplier used in the integrated proof. The monotonicity estimate for uniqueness makes no additional choices.
thm-projected-euler-square-root-global-e:
## Statement

Assume the hypotheses of [[thm-projected-euler-existence-uniqueness-and-convergence]], including Countable Choice and Dependent Choice, and let $x$ be its unique solution. Let $D$ be any finite bound for the diameter of $C$, set
$$M=\|f(0,x_0)\|_2+L(T+D),\qquad C_0=8M^2+L^2(1+M)^2T,\qquad C=\sqrt{C_0T e^{(2L+1)T}}.$$
For $h=T/N$, let $X_h$ be the affine interpolant of the exact projection Euler recurrence. If a complete run of [[alg-certified-projected-euler-method]] returns nodes $\widetilde x_k$ with certified residuals
$$\sup_{z\in C}\langle \widetilde x_k+h f(t_k,\widetilde x_k)-\widetilde x_{k+1},z-\widetilde x_{k+1}\rangle\le\varepsilon_k^2,$$
and $\widetilde X_h$ is their affine interpolant, then
$$\sup_{0\le t\le T}\|\widetilde X_h(t)-x(t)\|_2\le C\sqrt h+e^{LT}\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}\varepsilon_k.$$
In particular, the exact-projection branch has uniform error $O(\sqrt h)$. Certified projection errors with $\sum_k\varepsilon_k=O(\sqrt h)$ retain that rate; no rate follows from an uncertified solver tolerance alone.
